# Instructor guide · Topic 18: Advanced Graphs

<!-- generated by tools/export-docs.mjs from topics/ and questions/: do not edit by hand -->

## Learning objectives

Order tasks with topological sort, detect cycles, track connectivity with union-find, find weighted shortest paths with Dijkstra, and build minimum spanning trees with Prim and Kruskal.

By the end of the topic, students can:

- **Topological sort:** In a directed acyclic graph (DAG), order the nodes so every edge points forward.
- **Detecting cycles:** Directed graphs: DFS with three colors; reaching a gray node (still on the current path) means a cycle.
- **Union-find:** A forest of parent pointers that answers “are a and b connected?” and merges groups, in almost O(1) per operation with path compression and union by size.
- **Dijkstra's shortest paths:** With non-negative weights, always settle the unsettled node with the smallest known distance (a min-heap gives it to you), then relax its edges.
- **Negative weights: Bellman-Ford:** Dijkstra breaks when an edge can lower the cost of an already settled node.
- **Minimum spanning trees:** Connect every node with the least total edge weight.

## Duration and prerequisites

- Lessons: about **68 minutes** of guided material (6 lessons)
- Practice: 13 coding problems and 31 quick questions in the bank; plan at least as much practice time as lesson time
- Suggested format: one 90-minute session
- Prerequisites: Topic 17 (Graphs), Topic 15 (Heap / Priority Queue)

## Live coding demonstrations

- Bellman-Ford (lesson “Negative weights: Bellman-Ford”)
- Brute force → optimal walkthrough: **Weighted shortest path: BFS → Dijkstra** (Challenge tab). Code the brute force, ask students to find the repeated work, then refactor.
- Visualizers to drive while students predict the next step: Advanced graph algorithms

## Questions to ask the class

Ask, wait for several answers, then reveal (the answers are on the topic's Review flashcards).

- Topological order exists iff…
- Kahn's algorithm?
- Directed cycle check?
- Union-find ops?
- Dijkstra requires…
- Negative weights?
- Prim vs Kruskal?

## Classroom exercises (individual, 10–15 minutes each)

- Use the lesson questions.

Code tracing on the board: Kahn’s algorithm (`ag-p1`), Dijkstra result (`ag-p2`), Counting groups (`ag-p3`), Kahn’s algorithm by hand (`ag-dr1`)

Find-the-bug warm-ups: BFS on weighted edges (`ag-d1`), Union without find (`ag-d2`)

## Pair programming (25–30 minutes)

One driver types, one navigator thinks ahead and checks edge cases; swap every 10 minutes.

- Course Schedule (`ag-can-finish`)
- Course Schedule II (`ag-course-order`)
- Build from scratch: Build Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union) (`build-union-find`)

## Homework

- Cycle in a Directed Graph (`ag-cycle-directed`)
- Cycle in an Undirected Graph (`ag-cycle-undirected`)
